This is the game I sought refuge after feeling abandoned in Destiny 2 and discouraged in Warframe. No cut content, no dlc required, no confusing maps. The whole game is very clear and precise in what you need to do and provides a wiki by itself not requiring external websites. TL;DR: Warframe/Destiny knock off is actually fun. Doesn't have the same level of polish.

The First Descendant is a fairly good game that brazenly copies elements from Destiny and Warframe. The problem with directly copying these games is that you can't help but to compare every single element to them.

TFD gets the core gameplay right (thank god), which makes it fun to play. Compared to Warframe though, the guns, movement, and customization don't feel *quite* as good. The drop rates feel a bit too low and microtransactions are just a bit too expensive. It makes the game feel like a knock off. If Nexon decides to take development seriously, then this game could become one of the greats. In it's current state, it's good enough if you're tired of Warframe and Destiny.

Played 500 hours on record so far. For all the problems this game has, its bravery to be outwardly sexual isn't one of them. Season 3 Episode 4 has brought with it sweeping changes that greatly reduces the tedium of certain aspects in the game. While the loot is still not as plentiful as it should be, there is enough here to satisfy a MMO player for a decent stretch of time.

The only complaint I still have that I find to be the top 1 issue that needs to be addressed is the optimization and performance. The game is unstable and requires a full from the top clean up for even at 1080p medium-high settings, the game is struggling to keep a stable 60 frames when its competitors are easier to run and far more varied and captivating graphically,

If u can run it give the game a shot, the game has scale, the cool factor and build variety of its peers like Destiny and Warframe; games that have had a decade to refine and learn. If u don't have any qualms against the outwardly sexual design of its female characters then this is a decent MMO in a space where most die; this one is still trying and listening.

The latest patches have added a lot of friction to the game, and it’s no longer enjoyable. Farming is expected, but with every update they add another bleak map that you have to run a hundred times just to get one item you probably don’t even need. For the last three seasons, the game has basically forced players to use Serena because everything else feels weak in comparison.

They introduced some “rebalancing,” but it’s nowhere near enough. The so-called “new” content still has spongy bosses that require heavily optimized builds, and the only real tankiness still comes from Serena.

They also added swords, and they’re a complete mess. Swords require ammo and even share ammo with rocket launchers, which makes no sense. Ammo-generation skills don’t work while a sword is equipped, and heavy attacks often swing in random directions instead of toward the targeted boss.

Players used to complain that new weapons and descendants were overpowered; now the new stuff isn’t even worth farming, and Serena remains OP. It feels like the devs have gotten lazy and are only focused on what new skin they can sell next, forgetting that players need fun, engaging content before they’ll want to spend money on cosmetics.

I enjoyed The First Descendant at first. The gameplay is decent and the combat is solid, but it quickly became repetitive and grind-heavy. The world feels empty and lifeless, with very little NPC presence or immersion outside of missions.

The monetization is also very aggressive, constantly pushing purchases and making progression feel unnecessarily slow without spending money. On top of that, the heavy sexual fan service felt overdone and distracting rather than adding anything meaningful.

Overall, it looks great on the surface, but it ends up feeling hollow and overly focused on monetization instead of depth or world-building.

Even with meeting system requirements, this game acted like it wanted to explode my PC. I don't think I've ever touch a more unoptimized game in my entire life.

It's a loot/grind treadmill so if that's the sort of thing you're into then I'm sure you'll have a great time. Likewise, if you're not into these sorts of games or this genre then this game is unlikely going to convince you otherwise.

The only real downside at the moment is that content feels very finite and it's even pretty scarce compared to it's more established competitors. Once you participate in a new piece of content, it won't take you long to farm up all you can get from it and to take a favorite character to their peak performance. This climb is also lessened if you're not a collector who isn't interested in grinding out and developing each character or their weapons which leaves a lot of players out to dry while they wait for the next content drop.

If you meet the game on it's own terms, there definitely fun to be had. If you're a fan of the genre, keep an eye on this game a year or two from now as more content gets added.
